strings.name: Lars Peter Hansen
strings.summary: Hansen connects statistical inference with dynamic economic models. His generalized method of moments uses model restrictions and data to estimate and test parameters. With Jagannathan and others he studied asset-pricing restrictions, and with Sargent explored model uncertainty and robust decisions. A longtime Chicago professor, he shared the 2013 economics Nobel. A 2026 working paper examines climate uncertainty and policy valuation.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Developed the generalized method of moments, applying statistical inference to asset pricing and macroeconomics.
strings.facts.f1.label: Upbringing
strings.facts.f1.value: Grew up in Logan, Utah, where his father worked at Utah State University.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Mathematics and political-science BS, Utah State (1974); economics PhD, Minnesota (1978).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Generalized method of moments
strings.highlights.h1.text: Connected economic models and data through testable moment conditions, creating a widely used estimator.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Risk and model uncertainty
strings.highlights.h2.text: Studies asset-price restrictions, long-run risks and decisions robust to misspecified models.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Updated climate-policy working paper
strings.timeline.t1.text: With Barnett, Brock and Zhang, examined deep uncertainty, emissions, research investment and social valuation.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Shared economics Nobel
strings.timeline.t2.text: Won with Eugene Fama and Robert Shiller for empirical analysis of asset prices.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Nemmers Prize in Economics
strings.timeline.t3.text: Northwestern recognized his econometric and economic research.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Asset-pricing bounds paper
strings.timeline.t4.text: With Ravi Jagannathan, used market data to bound the variability of stochastic discount factors.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Foundational GMM paper
strings.timeline.t5.text: Published large-sample properties of generalized method-of-moments estimators in Econometrica.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined Chicago
strings.timeline.t6.text: Moved from Carnegie Mellon to begin a long research and teaching career in Chicago.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Doctorate and first faculty job
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earned an economics PhD at Minnesota before joining Carnegie Mellon.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed Utah State studies
strings.timeline.t8.text: Combined mathematics and political science, linking quantitative methods with social-science interests.
